svg.title: Identity isolation lab — detailed architecture
svg.text: Subnets, route tables, Transit Gateway route-table wiring, and the DNS path from the workload account to the domain controllers.

g.text: DHCP option set → domain controller DNS
single, shared — the only path to the internet

svg.text: reserved — no NAT in this AZ

g.text: network VPC attachment · associated with the shared table
default association and propagation both disabled
workload VPC attachment · accepted in the network account
private subnets only · no internet gateway · no NAT

svg.text: Resolving corp.theuptimestudio.co from the workload account
The instance asks the Amazon resolver at 10.30.0.2 — the workload VPC keeps the default DNS server.
A Route 53 Resolver rule, shared by RAM and associated with this VPC, matches the AD zone.
Traffic crosses the Transit Gateway on the spoke route table.
The rule's outbound endpoint, in the network VPC, forwards the query onward.
The domain controllers answer. Everything else resolves normally through the Amazon resolver.
AWS RAM · associated with the workload VPC
Directory security group opened to each spoke CIDR on the AD ports only — no RDP, no SSH.
